title: Composing Task-specific Agent Harnesses at Test Time with Reusable Primitives
abstract: arXiv:2609.38912v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent harnesses govern how large language models (LLMs) gather context, invoke tools, verify results, preserve state, and terminate, largely affecting agent performance. However, the value of each harness mechanism can differ across heterogeneous tasks: a mechanism that improves one task may impose overhead or context distraction on another, leading to the suboptimality of a global harness. We characterize this suboptimality as a mismatch induced by fixed mechanism choices, motivating task-specific harness construction. Nonetheless, generating harness code for each task introduces generation and debugging costs, with execution risks that can compound as more mechanisms are generated. To address those challenges, we introduce Harness Primitives, reusable harness mechanisms with clear application scope and composition contract mined from failed task trajectories. translated_title: 在测试时利用可重用原语组合任务特定的智能体执行框架
translated_abstract: 智能体执行框架决定了大语言模型（LLM）如何收集上下文、调用工具、验证结果、保存状态以及终止运行，在很大程度上影响智能体的性能。然而，每种框架机制的价值在不同异构任务之间可能存在差异：能够改善某一任务的机制可能对另一任务造成开销或上下文干扰，从而导致全局统一框架的次优性。我们将这种次优性刻画为由固定机制选择所引起的不匹配，进而激发了构建任务特定框架的动机。尽管如此，为每个任务生成框架代码会引入生成与调试成本，且随着生成机制的增多，执行风险会不断叠加。为应对这些挑战，我们提出了Harness Primitives（框架原语），这是一组从失败任务轨迹中挖掘出的、具有明确适用范围和组合契约的可重用框架机制。基于Harness Primitives，我们提出了STITCH框架，该框架能够为任务选择合适的原语并进行组合……
tldr: 提出从失败任务轨迹中挖掘可重用的框架原语，并构建STITCH框架在测试时为特定任务动态组合智能体执行框架，从而避免全局统一框架的次优性以及逐任务生成框架代码的成本与执行风险。
en_tdlr: Proposes Harness Primitives—reusable harness mechanisms mined from failed task trajectories—and STITCH, a framework that composes task-specific agent harnesses at test time, avoiding the suboptimality of a global harness and the generation costs and execution risks of per-task harness code.
